title: The Dance Architect
story:
Dance had always been at the heart of Jung Hoseok's identity. But when he joined BTS, he discovered that being a great dancer was only one part of what it took to create a powerful group performance.

During the trainee years, j-hope began taking responsibility for leading dance practices. He understood that some of the members had less experience with dancing, and he wanted to help them improve while making sure they could enjoy the process. He often took the lead in learning choreography and helping the others get the movements right.

In a 2014 interview, j-hope explained that he felt a sense of responsibility: if he became lazy about dancing, the other members might become less motivated too. He wanted to set an example and help everyone develop their skills.

Over time, this role became an important part of BTS's performance identity. j-hope paid attention not only to his own movements but also to the group's timing, formations, details, and synchronization. He regularly monitored performances and looked for ways to make them better.

In a 2019 interview, he described himself as the choreography team leader, while also acknowledging how much he continued to learn from the other members. 

For j-hope, the most important thing was never simply to make himself stand out. The team had to move with the same mindset. Every member needed to understand their role, and every movement had to contribute to the energy of the group.

That is what makes his role so special. He is not just someone who knows the choreography. He helps shape the way BTS performs together, encouraging the members, noticing the details, and pushing the group to give their best.

A great performance is built one movement at a time — and j-hope has been helping BTS put those movements together for years.
surpriseDescription: A great performance takes teamwork, dedication and guidance. Watch j-hope in his element as he leads, teaches and helps his fellow members bring the choreography to life.

challenge.question: Why did j-hope feel responsible for leading dance practice during BTS's trainee years?
options: He wanted to make sure the other members stayed motivated and improved.
He wanted to choose all the members' stage outfits.
He wanted to perform every dance part by himself.
challenge.answer: He wanted to make sure the other members stayed motivated and improved.
challenge.explanation: j-hope said that he felt responsible for setting an example. He believed that if he became lazy about dancing, the other members might lose motivation too, so he worked hard to lead practice and help them improve.
